title.fallback: Proposal and pilot plan for {{ account.name }}

sub.fallback: The pilot plan is being prepared with {{ sender.name | default: 'our team' }}. Book the scoping call and it follows once the scope is agreed.

recipe.prompt:
Collect what our Knowledge says for a proposal from {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} to {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}). knowledge.scoped holds the items about {{ account.name }} only: call notes, transcripts, files, signals and facts. knowledge.stable holds our workspace items: instructions, company files and our offer. Each item is {citationId, kind, title, text}. Use nothing else.

Return JSON with these keys, each a string:
- notes: at most 8000 characters. What knowledge.scoped says about the deal with {{ account.name }}: their problem and what it costs them, the people on their side with their titles, what each one said, the numbers they gave, the dates agreed, the pilot dates and criteria discussed, and what happens next. Keep quotes word for word in double quotes, with who said them and when. Leave out anything about other companies.
- offer: at most 2000 characters. Our standard offer from knowledge.stable: what we sell, how a pilot runs, its length, fee, credit and success terms, the year-one prices with their periods, what is not included, the currency, tax and billing terms, and how long a proposal stays valid.
- our_team: at most 2000 characters. Who we put on a pilot, from knowledge.stable or knowledge.scoped: each person's name, title, role on the pilot and time.

Facts: copy, never add. Keep every name, number, price, date and quote exactly as the item writes it. Never estimate, round or fill a gap from what is typical. A key is an empty string when no item states it, and all three are empty strings when there are no items.

You are writing the first half of a formal proposal from {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} to {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}). {{ sender.name | default: 'The sender' }} sends it. The champion at {{ account.name }} forwards it inside their company, so it has to make sense to a CFO or a security lead who was not on our calls. Write in the third person about {{ account.name }} and "we" for {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }}.

Inputs: data.notes is what our Knowledge says about the deal with {{ account.name }}: call notes, transcripts and facts. data.offer is our standard offer. What we know about the account: account.industry and account.size_band. The person it is addressed to is {{ person.first_name | default: 'not named' }} {{ person.last_name }}, {{ person.title }}. Use facts from these inputs only. Never invent customers, people, numbers, dates, quotes or results. If data.notes says nothing about a deal with {{ account.name }}, return {} and nothing else.

Return JSON with these keys:
- title: at most 90 characters. What the account gets, in their words, like "Operations visibility across Brightwave's seven terminals". Not a product name and not a slogan.
- sub: 1 or 2 sentences, 40 to 260 characters: the pilot, where it runs, the criteria it has to meet, and what a year-one rollout would involve. End by saying the document is written to be forwarded and by naming who needs it, taken from the notes.
- valid_until: the date the proposal stops being valid, like "Nov 28, 2026". Take the validity window from data.offer or data.notes and the send date from data.notes. An empty string if either is missing.
- pilot_window: the 30-day pilot dates, like "Nov 18 to Dec 18", from data.notes. An empty string if the notes give none.
- problem_when: at most 48 characters, which calls the quotes come from, like "Calls of Oct 14 and 21".
- problem_lead: 1 sentence saying what we heard, on which dates, and that the quotes are as close to how they were said as our notes allow.
- quotes: 2 or 3 items {text, who, date}. text is a quote from data.notes, copied word for word, at most 240 characters; never rewrite, merge or invent a quote. who is the name and title of the speaker, as the notes give them. date is like "Oct 14". Return [] when the notes hold no quote.
- cost_source: one line naming the document or call the numbers below come from and when it was shared, like "From Dana's September exception log for Joliet, shared Oct 23." An empty string if cost_today is empty.
- cost_today: 0 to 3 items {value, label}. value is a number from data.notes, like "140", "58 h" or "6 of 12", at most 12 characters. label says what it counts, at most 110 characters. Use a number only when data.notes states it or when it is plain arithmetic on numbers the notes state; show the arithmetic in the label, like "at 25 minutes each". Use an empty list when the notes have no numbers.
- problem_close: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 320 characters, that say what the problem is and is not, from the notes. No blame.
- scope_lead: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 300 characters: what we propose, starting at the pilot site, and how it connects to their systems, from the notes.
- scope_in: 4 or 5 items, each at most 140 characters, what the pilot covers. Items come from the notes and data.offer only.
- scope_out: 2 to 4 items, each at most 140 characters, what stays out until year one. From the notes and data.offer only.
- scope_close: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 300 characters, on what year one adds if the pilot passes, from data.offer.
- pilot_lead: 1 sentence, at most 260 characters: the dates, the site, the team that runs it, how many criteria and what they are measured against.
- criteria: 3 or 4 items {name, baseline, target, measured_by}. name at most 80 characters and measurable. baseline is the number the notes give, or the plain state today ("None", "0 of 12") when the notes say there is nothing. target is specific, like "20 or fewer" or "90 percent". measured_by is where the number comes from, like "Customer service desk log", at most 60 characters. Take baselines only from data.notes. Set targets from what the notes say the account wants; where they give none, pick a modest target and say nothing more.
- pass_rule: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 420 characters. The pilot passes when most criteria are met across its last two weeks. Then say what happens if it does not pass: no year-one commitment and the pilot fee is the only cost, if data.offer says so.

Voice: one person writing to a colleague, formal enough to forward. Specific, plain, no selling.

Rules for every string: plain words and short sentences. No em dashes or en dashes (write "Nov 4 to Dec 22", never a dash between dates). No exclamation marks, no emoji, no hype words (unlock, leverage, seamless, robust, transform, game changer, cutting-edge). Never "real" as emphasis. No email addresses or phone numbers. Sentence case. Dates read like "Nov 4" or "Nov 28, 2026".

You are writing the second half of a formal proposal from {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} to {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}), sent by {{ sender.name | default: 'the sender' }}. The first half is written: data.criteria, data.scope_in and data.pilot_window. Write the plan, the team, the investment, the next steps and the sign-off lead. It is forwarded inside {{ account.name }}, so it has to read cold.

Inputs: data.notes is what our Knowledge says about the deal with {{ account.name }}. data.offer is our offer with the prices. data.our_team is who we put on a pilot. Use facts from these inputs only. Never invent people, roles, hours, dates or prices.

Return JSON with these keys:
- timeline_lead: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 300 characters: how many weeks from the scoping call to the decision on year one, and what runs in parallel so the pilot can start on time.
- timeline_span: the first and last dates of the timeline, like "Nov 4 to Dec 22".
- weeks: exactly 8 strings, the Monday of each of 8 consecutive weeks, like "Nov 2". The first week is the one that contains the scoping call. Two or three words at most, month then day.
- tasks: 5 to 8 rows {label, who, side, span, marks}. label at most 48 characters, who at most 40 characters (names or a team, first names are fine). side is "us" for work our team does and "them" for work on their side. The grid has 16 columns, 2 for each week: column 1 is the first half of week 1 and column 16 the second half of week 8. A bar row has span {start, end}: start is the first column, end is the column after the last one, so a bar that covers the whole of weeks 3 and 4 is {start: 5, end: 9}. A row of single-day events has marks, a list of columns, and no span. Put the pilot on its real dates, the weekly reviews as marks, the readout as one mark and the decision on year one as one mark. Place every row by the dates in data.notes and data.pilot_window. Never place a bar so it ends before it starts.
- timeline_note: 1 sentence, at most 220 characters, that says the diamonds are single-day events and names the date the decision keeps something inside the year, if data.offer has a credit. Otherwise only the first part.
- team_lead: 1 sentence, at most 200 characters: how many people, and about how many hours a week in total on their side, only if the notes allow the sum.
- team: 5 to 8 rows {name, title, role, time}. Their people come from data.notes, ours from data.our_team, theirs first. title is "<title>, <company>". role is at most 140 characters, what the person does in the pilot. time is at most 40 characters, like "2 h a week", from the inputs only; write "As needed" when none is given.
- investment_lead: 1 sentence, at most 260 characters: the fixed pilot fee and how it is credited, from data.offer. An empty string when data.offer has no prices.
- investment: 2 to 4 rows {item, covers, amount}, built from data.offer. Copy every amount exactly as data.offer writes it, with its period ("$4,800", "$58,000 a year"). covers is at most 160 characters. Never round, add, convert or invent an amount. Return [] when data.offer has no prices.
- investment_total: {label, amount} for the line the offer calls the year-one price with the pilot credit applied. The amount is data.offer's own figure, or the plain difference of two figures it gives. Return {} when the offer states no credit.
- investment_note: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 300 characters: currency, tax, billing terms and any limit, from data.offer only. An empty string when data.offer states none of these.
- next_steps: 4 or 5 rows {date, title, detail}. date like "Nov 4". title at most 60 characters. detail at most 180 characters, who does what, using first names. Dates and owners come from data.notes; the last row is the kickoff.
- signoff_lead: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 260 characters: what the signature approves (the 30-day pilot and its criteria at the fee above) and that year one is a separate decision after the readout.

Voice: one person writing to a colleague, formal enough to forward. Plain, specific, no selling.

Rules for every string: plain words and short sentences. No em dashes or en dashes (write "Nov 4 to Dec 22", never a dash between dates). No exclamation marks, no emoji, no hype words (unlock, leverage, seamless, robust, transform, game changer, cutting-edge). Never "real" as emphasis. No email addresses or phone numbers. Sentence case. Dates read like "Nov 4" or "Nov 28, 2026".

recipe.rubric:
Grade this proposal the way the account's CFO or security lead reads it: cold, forwarded by a champion, looking for what is promised and what it costs. 10 is a document they approve without a call.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- grounded: every name, date, number and quote traces to the notes, the offer or the team list below. A quote must be word for word.
- measurable: each pilot criterion has a baseline, a target and a source, and the pass rule follows from them.
- consistent: the pilot dates, criteria, timeline rows, team, next steps and investment agree with each other. No bar ends before it starts, and every week label is a real Monday.
- plain: short sentences, plain words, no selling.
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, an exclamation mark, a hype word, an email address or phone number, an amount that data.offer does not state, a quote that is not in the notes, a number in cost_today or criteria that is not in the notes (or plain arithmetic on them), or a person who is not in the notes or the team list.
Deal notes: {{ data.notes }}
Offer: {{ data.offer }}
Our team: {{ data.our_team }}
Pass when the overall score is 7.5 or higher and no check is 6 or lower. On a fail, name the check and quote the phrase or number to change. The fix never supplies replacement names, numbers, quotes or prices.
